cells.tense: You are here at the closing of something, still open to what is coming next.
cells.ask: Name one thing you know is finished, say it out loud to yourself, and leave the door open on what replaces it.
cells.core:
You finish things. Not just tick them off — you carry them until they're whole, and then you let the next one arrive. That's rarer than it sounds, and rarer still that you don't stall at the end holding on.

What good looks like here: a cycle closes and you're already standing in the space it left. You can tell what's worth walking toward before you can explain why, and that read lands often enough that you trust it. So the finish doesn't shut anything down. Nothing gets skipped and nothing gets dragged past its end. You complete, and then you're free to meet what's arriving.
cells.sheetLine: You finish what's yours and stay open to what's next.

cells.tense: You will have declared this finished before it has actually finished becoming.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are calling done and do one more day of work on it before you set it down.
cells.core:
You've already decided how this ends. The next phase is written in your head, the arrival is on the calendar, and you're acting like you're standing past the finish line when you're still a fair way from it.

The instinct is good. You can see the shape of the completion — that's the same sight that serves you when it's working. Right now you're using it to skip the last part of the walk. Calling it done early robs the finish of its weight, and you miss the moment where the thing actually becomes yours. Wait until it's finished and you'll have something real to release rather than a story about finishing.

cells.tense: You were part of something that closed and you have not let it close.
cells.ask: Say the phrase 'that is gone now' about one thing you are still waiting to come back, out loud, once.
cells.core:
There's a room you keep standing in. Something ended — some part of you knew — and you didn't let it finish, so you're still there in a way, waiting for the next phase to kick in, still looking for the piece that would make it whole.

Spotting what matters isn't the problem here. You're not lost, and you're not short on knowing. What's missing is letting something be over. You've kept it open — maybe closing would mean it mattered, maybe the next thing hasn't shown up yet, maybe closing is just hard. Standing in that doorway is costing you the next room.
cells.sheetLine: You're standing in a doorway that closed behind you.

cells.tense: You are steering by it right now without having claimed it as yours.
cells.ask: Tell someone one call you made this week that came from that read, and say plainly that it was yours.
cells.core:
You act on what you notice. When you decide what to spend an hour on, who to call back, what to let slide — something in you knows before you can argue for it, and it steers most of the day. Credit goes somewhere else, though. 'The project needs this,' you say, or 'it just made sense.'

Your read isn't the issue. It's working, and it's yours. What hasn't happened is saying so — that you're the one who noticed, the one who made the call. When you take that back, the completions already happening around you stop feeling like luck and start feeling like yours, and you get to keep choosing from there.
